svg.title: Cultivation and Application of Mindfulness & Alertness

g.text: Cultivation and Application of Mindfulness & Alertness
Desire for "the end of this entire mass of suffering & stress" [AN_nblm.txt, 17][MN_nblm.txt, 341].
Difficulty following a "perfect and pure holy life" without mindfulness & alertness [AN_nblm.txt, 137, 139].
Live a perfect & pure holy life
Dwell heedful, ardent, and resolute to release the mind and end effluents.
Guard the doors of one's senses and know moderation in eating.
Practice Sense Restraint & Moderation in Eating
Involves active cleansing of the mind during various watches of the day and night.
Continuous training is essential for acquiring and strengthening these qualities.
Stage 2: Developing Core Qualities (Mindfulness & Alertness, Concentration)
The mind, when freed from these defilements, becomes pliant, malleable,
and luminous, allowing it to be rightly concentrated for the ending of effluents.
Mindfulness and alertness are developed in the context of concentration,
making the mind pliant, malleable, luminous, and not brittle. This includes
attending to the themes of concentration, uplifted energy, and equanimity.
A monk sits, holds the body erect, and establishes mindfulness to the fore,
breathing in and out mindfully, sensitive to the entire body, calming bodily
fabrications, being sensitive to the mind, gladdening, steadying, and releasing
the mind, and focusing on inconstancy, dispassion, cessation, and relinquishment.
Stage 3: Applying Mindfulness & Alertness in Practice
Making oneself alert in virtually all bodily movements and states:
going forward and returning, looking toward and away, bending and extending limbs,
carrying one's robes and bowl, eating, drinking, chewing, tasting, urinating,
defecating, walking, standing, sitting, falling asleep, waking up, talking,
Crucial for focusing on the body, feelings, mind, and mental qualities
"in & of itself," subduing greed and distress. This practice is described as
the "direct path for the purification of beings."
Mindfulness is explicitly listed as the first of the seven factors for awakening,
which are developed to bring clear knowing and release to culmination.
For a monk intent on heightened mind, regularly attending to the themes of
concentration, uplifted energy, and equanimity ensures the mind becomes
pliant, malleable, and luminous, suitable for ending effluents.
When evil thoughts arise, a monk uses alertness to identify them and then
redirect attention to skillful themes or scrutinize the drawbacks of the
unskillful thoughts, thereby abandoning them and concentrating the mind.
The mind is made pliant, malleable, luminous, and not brittle,
leading to a mind rightly concentrated for the ending of effluents.
Helps in cleansing the mind of qualities that would hold it in check,
such as sensual desire, ill will, sloth & drowsiness, restlessness & anxiety, and uncertainty.
Developing mindfulness immersed in the body helps conquer displeasure,
delight, fear, and dread, and prevents memories and resolves related to
household life from interfering with concentration.
Mindfulness and alertness are a development of concentration that leads
to mindfulness and alertness itself, implying a deepening of these qualities.
It is conducive to the attainment of the right method and the realization of unbinding.
For those in training, it can lead to gnosis right here and now, or non-return
if there is any remnant of clinging.
